utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Notwithstanding the nocturnal activities, no sleep will be tolerated in court this morning. Mr. Alarid, I have considered your submissions with regard to the continuation of your cross-examination, and I'll give you another 15 minutes, but, of course, following the conclusion of Mr. Cepic's cross-examination. Mr. Cepic shouldn't have much more to cross-examine on. I want to say that this witness has obviously been through a lot of trauma, and she obviously should be given the consideration that that requires. Mr. Cepic, let us hear from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours and thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, madam. I hope you are well rested now. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can hear you. You can go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to retrieve 0064-1874 to be shown on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't have the numbers memorized. Is this the video or is it the transcript?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Just the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, just so the Chamber knows, I spoke with Mr. Cepic after yesterday's court session, and the Prosecution agrees with to his tendering of the video and I ask that it not be shown again in court. We will agree that any videos, taped interviews that he wants to introduce in evidence. We will not object to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have the second page, please, in B/C/S, and also in English. [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, if it is possible for the transcript not be shown outside the courtroom because of a mention of a name.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Madam, there is mention here of a male nurse who cleaned your wound and who gave you bandages and medicines. You can see that towards the top of the page. You will agree with me that here you describe the gentleman code named VG-32.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, madam.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, at the beginning of the page when the journalist asks you, "Did you recognise any of the criminals then," you answered: "These were just whipper-snappers. Some of them not only were nearly drunk, they were drugged as well. That's how terrible their conduct was. There was an elderly man there."

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: This elderly man, he was 20 to 30 years your senior, was he not?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you his exact age.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Approximately, what was the difference between your ages, 20, 30 years?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe around 50.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Was his hair grey?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in such terror, do you think I had the time to observe the colour of his hair?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I fully understand you. So because of the fear and the terrible situation, you could not notice any of the details pertaining to that person; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a big man, around 50 years of age; he wore a uniform that is still worn by the army, and his trouser legs were open; and his hair was brownish, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did you notice whether he sported a mustache or a beard?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The gentleman did not sport a mustache. Wait. I know this man, he hales from Visegrad, but I cannot recall his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Please tell me, that group that came, did they wear any hats or caps?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I no longer recall whether they wore any such head gear or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And those young men, you call them "whipper-snappers," how much older were you from them?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not say that all of them were my juniors. I knew that Milan Lukic, whom I knew, that he was younger than me. As for the rest of them --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, madam. I will no longer upset you about this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I am sorry. I didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Could I ask admission of this transcript related to which we broadcasted yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no objection to that. I'd only ask that the video that accompanied the transcript, which is the original as the best evidence, be also admitted, so that the Chamber is free to view the video should it choose to do so in deliberations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, that is to be done.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit number 2D37.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have in e-court system 2D03-0068.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, madam, while waiting for the document to be shown up, you remember that on the 15th and 16th of December 1992, you had a discussion with Mr. Dermot Groome and another investigator and interpreter (redacted). On the 15th, you met around 2.00 p.m., and on the 16th of December at around 4.00 p.m. at your home?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall the visit to my home, but I cannot remember the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have the second page, please. Scroll down, please. Thank you. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And you provided a description to Mr. Groome, and you said that Milan Lukic and another six persons from Obrenovac came there?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You also stated that there were members of the Savic family among them; that's bullet point 3.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I ask admission of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I ask that to be under seal. It contains the name of a protected witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be Exhibit number 2D38, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And just for the record, related to the previous video which is admitted, there are some technical problems with the copy. I think that Mr. Groome is familiar with that, so I expect that we'll have the full version of that video in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with specifically with what Mr. Cepic is referring to, but I'm happy to discuss that during the break, and I'm sure it can be resolved.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Could we have Exhibit 2D04-0129, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, while we are waiting for this to show up, do you remember Dr. Harem Hodzic from the Zenica hospital at all?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember Mr. Hodzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have the third page.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, I'm showing you an interview to Oslobodjenje on the 22nd of May 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have the next page, please, bottom of the page, in B/C/S; in English, that would be the last page.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, in this interview, you mention many names; Mile Joksimovic, Dr. Radomir Vasiljevic are also mentioned; a policeman from Visegrad by the name of Tomic; and some others. And, finally, it is claimed that those were your words concerning the incidents at Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you who I do remember now. I remember Mitar Vasiljevic, he was a waiter in Visegrad; I remember Mile Joksimovic, but I can't recall what his profession was; Dr. Vasiljevic is the doctor who came to the house I was at, to bring me medicine; Dragan Sekovic is my neighbour, I can't recall whether I discussed him at all; and his brother Dragomir as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic -- Witness, are you finished?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just want to say what I said in terms of which persons I knew to have committed crimes. I cannot recall that I mentioned all these names that appear here on this list in this publication, and, thereby, I answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, madam. Can we request admission of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Cepic, these matters don't essentially relate to your case, and I suspect you are doing it on behalf of Mr. Alarid. You would have observed that I have given Mr. Alarid another 15 minutes, so I suggest that you stop and let Mr. Alarid take over his own case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, with all due respect, 15 minutes wouldn't cover an additional time with this witness; and for all practical purposes, I wish it would, but just the nature of the proceedings makes that difficult under most circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, let the record be quite clear on this, the Prosecutor had two hours and ten minutes. In total, you had two hours and 40 minutes. It's really a matter for you to choose how you manage your time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, but I mean, by analogy, Your Honour, Mitar Vasiljevic was on the stand for 21 hours total. I didn't break down what was Mr. Domazet's direct exam and what was the Prosecution's cross-examine, but different witnesses have different importances, of course, to the case. Different witnesses, just by the virtue of the Prosecution's presentation, well, they can't constrain the cross by limiting their direct. I guess they could, but in certain instances, it just takes more time. That was my original point and it continues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm, in principle, quite opposed to time limits. We don't really have it in the system out of which I come.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Mine neither.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But it is necessary here. I've grown to understand in the ten years that I am here that it is absolutely necessary, and you must make the best use of the time that I have given you. So go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the documents tendered by Mr. Cepic will be assigned Exhibit number 2D39.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I was trying to sort myself, Your Honour. Excuse me for a moment. Could the court assistant please bring P138 back to the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, ma'am, while we are waiting for that, I would like to ask you, in the transcript of the witness interview -- excuse me, the journalist witness interview that Mr. Cepic just showed you, there was a passage in there, and I'll ask you if you recall it, regarding your statements to the Serbian guards and the authorities. It would be my position that in Exhibit P66 of the Prosecution, you originally told them that that journalist that you had told people that you had epilepsy and an accident related to that epilepsy. However, in the most recent document that was just entered as 2D37, it's a little bit shorter than that. It says: "I told them that I had a fit and that I tripped over a butane bottle and burnt myself." Do you recall, ma'am, telling Serbian people that right after you were burned and including the doctor?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, we are coming back to Bikavac, and I will describe the scene when I came to the command post of the Uzice Corps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and when I asked --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, no. Please don't answer yet, just listen to what I have to say. What the counsel is asking you is whether you remember saying in a statement to the guards that you had a fit and that you had tripped over a butane bottle and burnt yourself. Do you remember saying that in a statement to the guards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, first of all, I would like to tell you I do not suffer from epilepsy, and I can tell you that I never uttered those words anywhere in my life. And as far as this other thing is concerned, I cannot remember exactly what was going on over there. If I even said that, I probably tried to say something, but it was impossible for me to have done that. What is sure is one thing, I just wanted to see my destroyed life ended because there was nobody to take care of me and to help me survive at that moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that moment, I may have said that I was burned somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, continue please. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was maybe out of fear so that the Serbs would not torture me even more because I was already tortured too much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, did you put the statement to her yesterday? Did you show her the statement yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I believe we put P66 on the screen. This is another -- there was three videos of this woman after the war, sort of documentaries, journalist-type stuff, and she gave three. I believe all three are now in evidence and the Prosecution can assist me. I have a note, but I've been notoriously wrong, with P130 for transcript number 2. I could be totally wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, what do you mean when you just answered me by saying that at that moment you may have said that you were burned somewhere else? Can you explain that to me? Then you continued to say that that was perhaps out of fear so that the Serbs would not torture you even more, as you were already tortured too much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On that night when I was burned, everything was too much for me; and if I were to say the Serbs -- tell the Serbs that I had been burned by the Serbs, I was afraid that they would torture me even more before they kill me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see. Okay. Mr. Alarid, what you are actually putting to her is that she did not sustain her injuries as a result of the Bikavac fire --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: That she had an accident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: -- but as a result of an accident.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Do you understand that that is his case? His case is that you didn't suffer these injuries that you have, these terrible awful injuries, as a result of the Bikavac fire, but as a result of an accident, tripping over butane. He is entitled to put that to you because that is his case, so this is why we have to hear what your explanation is. You have explained that you suffered immensely at the time, and you feared that if you told the Serbs that you suffered the injury as a result of the fire at Bikavac, that they might torture you even more. I understand that to be the explanation for the statement that you made to the guards, that you had suffered the injuries as a result of an accident. Now, that's my understanding. Mr. Alarid, if you have more questions to put to her.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I do, a few, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please understand, and don't be upset. He is entitled to put these questions to you. In my view, it's an important issue, and that's primarily why I have allowed him to continue his cross-examination this morning. But we don't have all day. Remember the time constraint, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Is the Court's questioning part of mine?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, no. You have another eight minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Ma'am, do you see the photograph on the screen?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, according to your earlier testimony, you indicated that you were able to slip through a similar, if not identical, opening.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I'll give you the page number, Mr. Groome, which is at page 2320, lines 23 to 25 and 232 1, lines 1 to 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: "Can you compare what you were looking at here in terms of what you recall from that night?" Your answer: "They are exactly identical in terms of colour, exactly identical to the door by which I passed, and I went through an opening. That is exactly the same." Do you remember saying that, ma'am, in court? And as you look at the picture, can you tell me at all if this is the same door or just a very similar door?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, it goes for a similar door through which I emerged from there, or maybe identical, but I cannot confirm that to you now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, ma'am, isn't it true that according to your testimony, you were the last -- one of the last, if not the last people put into the Meho Aljic home?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I'm the only person who emerged through that door alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So that would mean you were right next to the door as it was put -- and let me ask you this, ma'am: Of the entry that you went into the Meho Aljic house, did it require both of these doors, because they're double doors, propped up against the opening to cover it, or was one of these doors sufficient to cover the opening?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, what I remember at this time about that door is that it was one garage door, dark red, and there were openings towards the top of approximately 60 centimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Ma'am, the reason I ask you is that is the image I got me my head from your earlier testimony regarding the opening that was covered by the garage door, it seemed like it was a wider opening. I think it was called a -- like it was a balcony or a double door opening. Is that true? Tell me what you recall about the opening that you were forced into.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I entered Meho Aljic's house through the balcony door and window.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, ma'am, wouldn't it be true that that is a wide opening, like a patio door?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a normal size door together with a window.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so, ma'am, wouldn't it be true that you would need both of those doors to cover that size of an opening; "those" being the garage doors in the picture?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not talking about two doors, just one door.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Ma'am, as the door --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Pause.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Ma'am, as the door was propped in front of the opening that you were at, how long did it take from you being inside the home to the door blocking the exit.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And the reason I ask you that is I envision a situation of a room full of people with you being closest to the door just because of the number of people in the room, and so it feels to me that you would be in the best position to have seen the placement of the door and that sequence of events that led to the door being put in front of that opening that everyone had been brought through. Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, she was asked a question about the door. She said she doesn't know. I'm not sure what Mr. Alarid's musing about why she may have seen the door is really relevant. She simply said she doesn't know. I suggest we move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We must move on unless you can explain the relevance, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I am a real visual person, and what I try and do through my cross-examination is provide an image. And if the image doesn't make sense, well, then, that becomes part of the argument of the case. The image I got, if I'm a victim at the door, I think I'd notice the sequence of events being trapped in this house, that timing of where there's light and then there's none, and there's opening and then it's gone. That's a very powerful moment to me as I relive this witness's story, so it's that where I find the relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, it's a little farfetched. Please move on, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How long were you in the home before you noticed that your exit was completely blocked off by the garage door?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was standing in the door inside the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, ma'am, isn't it true --

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see that the door and the window were blocked --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, ma'am, just looking --

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- by the garage door. But I do know exactly where the exit was, and I wanted to get out with my baby sister, whom I was holding in my arms. I wanted to get her out of the house. When I tried to escape, there was an obstacle that I ran into.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Ma'am, it would be easier if you --

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had to lower --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Ma'am, please --

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- my baby sister, put her down, leave her there inside the house near the garage door. And as soon as I was out of the house, I turned around in an attempt to see what had kept me, what sort of obstacle from escaping with my baby sister, and it was at that point that I saw the garage door blocking the way out.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay, ma'am. It would be much easier if you just answered my questions directly because I only have a very limited amount of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just another 2 minutes now, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I mean, that is my point, Your Honour. I asked her a yes-or-no question --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: -- and she goes on.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sorry. I must interject here. Mr. Alarid gave a lengthy question of what he imagined was going on inside the room. The witness has explained what was, in fact, going on inside the room, and what she saw inside the room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. She has explained as well as she is in a position to, Mr. Alarid. Please use the other 2 minutes well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: That's such a difficult thing. All right. Private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The next witness, Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution calls VG-131. I believe this witness has been granted protective measures of closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, closed session. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm going to give the outline of the Trial Chamber's reasoning in its decision on the Prosecution's motion for leave to amend the witness list by (redacted). Mr. Groome, should we be in private session for this?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness had indicated that it was his preference to testify openly and not use a pseudonym, but given the unique nature of this witness, if we could possibly refer to him by VG-138, just as a precautionary measure. I'm not sure what the decision is, but if he is not going to be called this week, it might prevent any possible interference with him between -- again, I'm not sure what the Chamber is going to decide, but maybe as a cautionary measure, we'd member refer to him by a pseudonym.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll do that, in which case the previous references should be redacted. The Chamber concludes that it is in the interest of justice to add Witness VG-138 to the Prosecution's witness list, also that the redacted information should be disclosed to the Defence, and that it is in the interest of justice to lift the ex parte status of all filings relating to the - I'll just repeat that - that is in the interest of justice to lift the ex parte status of all filings and that these will be recorded as confidential. However, in order to allow the Defence to properly examine this material, the witness will be called on Tuesday, the 11th of November. And in view of the fact that the stage of the proceedings is late, the examination of the chief will be restricted to matters arising out of the alibi of Milan Lukic. Consequently, the Chamber will grant the motion in part and order the Prosecution to add the witness to the witness list and to call that witness on the 11th of November, and to restrict the questioning to matters arising out of the Defence of Milan Lukic. As I said, we will be filing this very shortly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Now, in light of that, Mr. Groome, we envisage that the Prosecution would be closing its case after Witness VG-138.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: We would, Your Honour, we would be resting at that stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And we would then proceed to the 92 bis hearing immediately thereafter. That being the case, unless I'm mistaken, we would be adjourned until Tuesday. Next Tuesday? May I inquire what time? I'm told it's p.m., which means 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 11th day of November, 2008, at 2.15 p.m. 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.23 p.m.
